## Slice contract

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Stable Slice ID | `ACI-S40` |
| Contract | `atlas-aci/slice.v1` — Atlas project adaptation around canonical Ramza EARS |
| State | Planned; implementation has not started |
| Phase | 4 — Shared operation |
| Release selection | Shared-operation milestone |
| Timebox | 5 engineering day(s); stop and report remaining scope at the limit |
| Risk | P0 |
| Audited Atlas baseline | `213fa1c713de060a1dddeef2dc4293301503a71d`; inspect actual HEAD again at pickup |
| Ramza source | [`38f380f`](https://github.com/Rynaro/Ramza/blob/38f380f31b57a3598490332bd6cd87c67aa2bb32/SPEC.md), package 1.1.0 |
| Criteria SHA-256 | `98cb89a8437eeb73ac0f70ccb2547db80fc2e050dd7293093c07bd8fb478ff16` |
| Suggested executor | Strong coding executor; independent checker for the computed full tier |

**Outcome:** Provide tested multi-principal isolation for an explicitly configured shared HTTP deployment.

**Why:** Filtering returned nodes is too late if traversal, ranking, caches or source resources already expose private evidence.

The Slice identity, receipt fields and retry protocol are Atlas conventions. Ramza supplies the EARS grammar and planning gates; it does not define a Slice runner. This issue is execution input, not a fabricated completed Ramza phase record.

## Stories

As an Atlas user or agent operator, I want this bounded outcome so that the graph evidence delivered to coding agents satisfies the acceptance criteria below.

## Dependencies

- [ACI-S13](https://github.com/Rynaro/atlas-aci/issues/35)
- [ACI-S30](https://github.com/Rynaro/atlas-aci/issues/51)
- [ACI-S39](https://github.com/Rynaro/atlas-aci/issues/60)

A closed predecessor issue is insufficient evidence by itself. Verify that its required interface and acceptance evidence exist on the actual execution base. If a dependency is missing, return `BLOCKED` with the exact missing capability.

## Scope

### Included

- One declared identity-provider integration with per-repository authorization.
- Authorization before traversal, ranking, resource reads and cross-repository expansion.
- Principal/scope-aware cache keys and revocation-safe cursor validation.
- Guard or disable every legacy tool at shared dispatch, including file/search/memex and opt-in execution routes.

### Excluded

- Building an identity provider
- Deploying or opening network access as part of this issue

### Declared implementation paths

- `mcp-server/src/atlas_aci/protocol/*`
- `mcp-server/src/atlas_aci/query/*`
- `mcp-server/src/atlas_aci/config.py`
- `mcp-server/tests/slices/test_s40_*.py`
- `docs/operations/*`

New module and fixture paths above are proposed targets. Existing behavior lives primarily in the audited implementation; do not perform an unrelated directory rewrite. Record any justified path change through a scope amendment before expanding the diff. Planning/receipt files belong under `.spectra/`. Run each Slice in an isolated branch/worktree; do not schedule overlapping declared paths concurrently without an explicit merge/ownership plan.

## Approach

1. Write the principal/repository policy contract and negative fixtures first.
2. Validate protocol credentials using the selected official flow.
3. Apply policy before every evidence access and bind caches/cursors to scope.
4. Exercise two users with overlapping and disjoint repository access.

## Acceptance Criteria

The following blocks use the canonical [Rynaro/Ramza EARS template](https://github.com/Rynaro/Ramza/blob/38f380f31b57a3598490332bd6cd87c67aa2bb32/templates/acceptance-criteria.md). Each `THEN` is one assertion. All named product tests are **tests to add in this Slice**, not claims that those tests already exist or pass.

<!-- criteria:start -->
### AC-S40-001 (unwanted-behavior)
GIVEN a principal lacks repository access
WHEN a query names that repository
THEN the repository traversal count SHALL be zero.
VERIFY: test: mcp-server/tests/slices/test_s40_contract.py::test_unauthorized_before_traversal

### AC-S40-002 (unwanted-behavior)
GIVEN a principal presents another scope source URI
WHEN resource retrieval runs
THEN Atlas SHALL reject the access.
VERIFY: test: mcp-server/tests/slices/test_s40_contract.py::test_resource_authorization

### AC-S40-003 (event-driven)
GIVEN two principals have different authorized scopes
WHEN both submit the same query text
THEN each cache lookup SHALL use its authorization scope identity.
VERIFY: test: mcp-server/tests/slices/test_s40_contract.py::test_cache_scope_isolation

### AC-S40-004 (unwanted-behavior)
GIVEN repository access is revoked after a cursor is issued
WHEN the cursor is resumed
THEN Atlas SHALL reject the continuation.
VERIFY: test: mcp-server/tests/slices/test_s40_contract.py::test_revoked_cursor

### AC-S40-005 (event-driven)
GIVEN a path reaches an unauthorized repository
WHEN cross-repository traversal runs
THEN the protected repository SHALL not be expanded.
VERIFY: test: mcp-server/tests/slices/test_s40_contract.py::test_cross_repo_scope

### AC-S40-006 (event-driven)
GIVEN principal, policy and snapshot are unchanged
WHEN the same read request is repeated
THEN the authorization decision SHALL be identical.
VERIFY: test: mcp-server/tests/slices/test_s40_contract.py::test_auth_replay

### AC-S40-007 (unwanted-behavior)
GIVEN an allowed query warmed a cache before repository access was revoked
WHEN the same principal repeats the query
THEN the response SHALL contain no evidence from the revoked repository.
VERIFY: test: mcp-server/tests/slices/test_s40_contract.py::test_cache_revocation

### AC-S40-008 (unwanted-behavior)
GIVEN a principal lacks access to the target repository
WHEN each legacy tool is invoked in a parameterized dispatch fixture
THEN repository read or execution activity SHALL remain zero for every denied tool call.
VERIFY: test: mcp-server/tests/slices/test_s40_contract.py::test_legacy_tool_boundary

### AC-S40-009 (unwanted-behavior)
GIVEN credentials are absent or invalid for shared mode
WHEN any repository operation is requested
THEN Atlas SHALL deny the request before repository access.
VERIFY: test: mcp-server/tests/slices/test_s40_contract.py::test_invalid_credentials

### AC-S40-RUN-01 (event-driven)
GIVEN the product criteria pass on a recorded output commit and the declared implementation inputs are unchanged
WHEN an executor re-enters this Slice with its verified completion receipt
THEN the tracked implementation content digest SHALL remain unchanged.
VERIFY: gate: capture a SHA-256 manifest of declared tracked implementation files before and after clean-worktree re-entry; require exact manifest equality and git diff --exit-code against the recorded output commit for those paths.

### AC-S40-RUN-02 (event-driven)
GIVEN a partial execution receipt exists for this Slice and the frozen criteria digest still matches
WHEN an executor resumes the interrupted Slice
THEN the slice_id plus criteria_sha256 execution identity SHALL remain unchanged.
VERIFY: gate: compare slice_id and criteria_sha256 in the interrupted and resumed receipts; require one authoritative receipt path for that identity.
<!-- criteria:end -->

## Agent execution and idempotent re-entry

1. Read the issue, repository instructions, current HEAD and predecessor evidence. Verify this issue's stable marker before creating branches, files or follow-up work. Use `aci-s40` as the work identity; do not create a second issue for the same Slice.
2. Materialize the plan at `.spectra/plans/aci-s40.md` and the exact bytes between the criteria markers at `.spectra/plans/aci-s40.criteria.md`. The criteria digest is the value in the contract table. Keep the planning state at `.spectra/plans/aci-s40.state.json` and the separate execution receipt at `.spectra/state/aci-s40.execution.json`.
3. On a fresh plan, use `ramza-rightsize` with observed scope/stakes, follow the required phase walk, and compute rubric scores with `ramza-score`. Record independent maker/checker evidence when the computed tier requires it. Declare the actual file scope with `ramza-drift`. Initialize state once only.
4. On re-entry, run `ramza-gate status --state <state>` and inspect the existing receipt. Verify any frozen criteria with `ramza-freeze --state <state> --criteria <criteria> --verify`. Do not replay initialization, force-reset state, re-advance completed phases, or perform an initial freeze again. An intentional criteria change uses `--amend --reason` and invalidates the previous completion identity.
5. Before implementation handoff, run the structural and EARS gates; freeze previously unfrozen criteria at Assemble. If emitting an ECL handoff, validate its full schemas and independently check the spec and criteria digests; the emission tool alone is not complete schema validation.
6. If the product checks and output digests already hold, verify the two execution criteria and return `ALREADY_SATISFIED` without another implementation diff. If partial work exists, reconcile actual state and resume only missing work. A stale receipt, changed criterion hash or conflicting output returns `BLOCKED` until the discrepancy is resolved; do not overwrite unrelated work.
7. Keep canonical outputs stable on identical inputs. Diagnostic durations and append-only audit entries may differ; they cannot change facts, stable identities, result ordering or completion identity. Wall-clock-truncated graph work is only replay-identical when its captured frontier is identical. Budget limits below the documented minimum envelope are rejected under the separately documented fixed error cap.
8. Use one executor allocation for the bounded Slice. Additional model/agent spend and live paid evaluation require a configured operator budget. At the timebox limit, return the completed checks, remaining gaps and a narrow proposed follow-up; never silently expand the Slice.

## Verification and completion receipt

From `mcp-server/`, add and run the product checks named above:

```bash
uv run pytest tests/slices/test_s40_contract.py -q
```

Run the repository-required lint/type/CI checks applicable to the changed paths. Use fixture assertions against observable behavior; do not satisfy a requirement with a mock of the behavior being verified. Real-host, compiler, filesystem and concurrency claims need the corresponding integration evidence. Then perform the no-op re-entry and interrupted-resume gates.

The authoritative execution receipt records `slice_id`, `issue_url`, `criteria_sha256`, `base_commit`, `output_commit`, `declared_paths`, `output_digests`, `status`, and one result per AC with its actual command, exit code and evidence location. Valid terminal outcomes are `COMPLETE`, `ALREADY_SATISFIED` or `BLOCKED`; partial progress uses `IN_PROGRESS`. This receipt is separate from Ramza's planning state.

Close the Slice only when all required ACs have observed evidence, relevant repository gates pass, the completion receipt matches the actual output, and implementation/verification changes are reviewable in one bounded PR. No release, deployment, automatic merge or unrelated repository mutation is included.

## Confidence

The issue is grounded in the pinned source audit and explicit design decisions. The Ramza confidence verdict must be computed from execution-time observations; no numeric score or completed phase walk is asserted here. EARS/structural lint establishes document shape, not implemented behavior.

## Rejected Alternatives

- A single issue for the entire work package: it would mix independent outputs and make retries ambiguous.
- Marking work complete from a plausible implementation or a lint-only pass: completion requires the named observed checks.
- Reusing a prior completion receipt after source/criteria drift: reconcile and revalidate the actual inputs first.

## Risks

- The audited base may differ from the execution base after predecessor merges; inspect current interfaces before modifying them.
- Proposed module boundaries may need a narrowly documented adjustment; amend scope instead of hiding a wider rewrite.
- Some evidence providers have incomplete coverage; preserve their unsupported/unknown states rather than converting them into resolved facts.
